items.q: What makes a health claim on this channel checkable?
items.a: It points at a study you can open and argue with. "It penetrates the cancerian shell" does not. A confident fake pH is the demo. [[fact-check-needs-a-study]].

items.q: What does he say colloidal silver does?
items.a: Nothing useful. HHS: no benefits, real risks, including skin turned blue. Airplane spray and a family throat spray are still exposure. [[colloidal-silver-no-benefit]].

items.q: Why is "eat 2,400, burn 400, therefore gain" wrong?
items.a: Exercise is not the whole burn. You burn calories while alive. He says that green-coffee study was retracted and the FTC followed. [[basal-burn-is-the-budget]].

items.q: When has a talk show started doing a doctor's job?
items.a: When it names the disease and the drug. Plavix with no exam. A past-life witch trial for anxiety. Leave. A Springer reunion can still be how a family finally got a diagnosis, and that is the failure. [[talk-show-is-not-a-clinic]].

items.q: Why is "not found in nature" not a safety test?
items.a: Folic acid prevents neural tube defects. Cyanide is natural. The guest already said he is not a doctor. That ends the segment.
